controls.name: Monitoring and alerting for export throughput and failures
controls.description: Operations documentation states that export throughput and failure rates are reported to an operations dashboard and that a failed export raises an alert.
limitations: Documentation does not state whether monitoring includes detection of anomalies that might indicate interception or tampering of internal export traffic.

mappings.applicability_reason: thr-005 involves only the customer-facing Export API, the internal Export Worker, and the managed object store (evd-001–evd-003). No privileged administrative or operator interface is involved in the described attack path, and the attacker’s foothold is at the network level rather than through administrative access, so controls on privileged administrative interfaces do not bear on interception of internal export traffic.

The architecture describes a simple export service that assembles and stores customer records for download (evd-001–evd-003), and thr-005 concerns interception of export traffic between these components. There is no indication that content is passed to any model, so controls for treating untrusted model input do not bear on this threat.
assumptions: Assume the export service does not call or embed any ML/AI models, because the architecture overview lists only an HTTP Export API, an internal Export Worker, and a managed object store (evd-001–evd-003).

mappings.applicability_reason: The threat thr-005 concerns interception and tampering of export traffic between the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store (evd-001–evd-003). No model output is described or published, so requirements about validating model output before external publication do not bear on this threat.
assumptions: Assume the export service does not generate or publish model output, as the documentation describes only exporting existing customer records (evd-001–evd-003).

mappings.applicability_reason: The system is described as assembling exports from existing customer records and writing them to a managed object store (evd-001–evd-003). There is no indication that customer content is sent to an external model provider, and thr-005 is about interception of export traffic rather than model-based processing, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.
assumptions: Assume the export service does not use any external model provider; the only external dependency mentioned in the export path is a managed object store (evd-003, evd-006).

mappings.applicability_reason: thr-005 describes interception or tampering of internal export traffic between services, not rendering of model output in a user interface. The architecture describes only export files assembled from customer records (evd-001–evd-003), so requirements about encoding model output for rendering do not bear on this threat.
assumptions: Assume no model-generated content is rendered in the Export Service user interface, since only export files of existing records are described (evd-001–evd-003).

mappings.applicability_reason: This requirement concerns documenting delegation of user authentication to an external identity provider. thr-005 assumes an attacker with internal network access who can intercept or tamper with traffic between internal components; whether customer authentication is local or delegated (ctl-003, evd-004) does not affect protection of those internal flows, so this requirement does not bear on the described threat.

req-AUTH-002 is about who enforces multi-factor authentication for administrative or privileged access. thr-005 concerns an attacker with internal network access intercepting traffic between services; it does not involve administrative logins or factor policy, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

The export service appears to support multiple customers ("customers" in evd-001), but thr-005 focuses on an attacker with internal network access observing or modifying export traffic between components. Tenant-aware authorization constrains which tenant’s data a given request may access, but it does not prevent a network-position attacker from eavesdropping on or tampering with traffic once generated, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-AUTHZ-002 concerns limiting delegated privileges when integrating with an external platform. The architecture for the export path mentions only an Export API, an internal Export Worker, and a managed object store (evd-001–evd-003); thr-005 concerns interception of traffic among these components, not misuse of delegated external privileges, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.
assumptions: Assume the export service does not act on customer resources on an external platform via delegated access, beyond storing export files in the managed object store described (evd-003, evd-006).

mappings.applicability_reason: req-CICD-001 addresses how the deployment pipeline authenticates to environments and how third-party components in the build are controlled. thr-005 is about runtime interception or tampering of export traffic between running components, not compromise of the deployment pipeline or build artifacts, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

The export service transmits and stores customer records and assembled export files (evd-001–evd-003), which are reasonably treated as confidential, and the Export API is a public HTTPS service (evd-002), so data crosses networks the system does not fully control. thr-005 specifically concerns disclosure and tampering when internal flows between the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store are not strongly encrypted or authenticated, directly engaging the requirement that sensitive data be encrypted in transit and at rest.
assumptions: Assume customer records and export files are considered confidential data for the purpose of applying encryption requirements, even though no explicit data_classification is recorded in the model (evd-001–evd-003).

mappings.applicability_reason: req-DATA-002 concerns how long sensitive working data is retained and whether that period matches customer-facing statements. thr-005 is about interception and tampering of export data in transit between components, which occurs regardless of whether completed export files are retained for 30 days or deleted immediately (evd-003, evd-006), so retention controls do not bear on this threat.

The managed object store holds export files for customers (evd-003, evd-006), likely across multiple customers, but thr-005 concerns an attacker intercepting or modifying data in transit between the Export Worker and the store, not unauthorized access via storage paths. Separating stored artifacts by tenant would not in itself prevent network interception of those writes, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-DATA-004 is about documenting how customer data can be deleted on request across all stores. thr-005 focuses on an attacker observing or tampering with export data in transit between internal components, not whether data can later be deleted, so this requirement does not bear on the described threat.

req-LOG-001 concerns excluding restricted data from application logs and documenting where logs are sent. thr-005 describes compromise via interception or modification of export traffic between services, not via logs, and the available documentation about logging relates only to monitoring throughput and failures (evd-007), so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-LOG-002 addresses recording security-relevant administrative actions. thr-005 does not involve any administrative interface or operator actions; the attacker’s capability is network interception between components, so administrative auditing does not bear on this threat.

The Export Worker and managed object store are internal components that hold export files on behalf of multiple customers (evd-001–evd-003, evd-006), and are not themselves described as public interfaces. thr-005 specifically considers an attacker with internal network access intercepting or tampering with traffic between these components, directly engaging the requirement that such internal stores and services be reachable only from the workloads that use them rather than from an untrusted network.

req-SECRET-001 is about storing long-lived signing keys and provider credentials in a managed secret store. thr-005 assumes an attacker with internal network access and focuses on lack of strong encryption or authentication on internal channels, not on theft or misuse of stored credentials, so this requirement does not bear directly on the threat.

req-SECRET-002 concerns using short-lived credentials when accessing customer resources on external platforms. thr-005 describes an attacker intercepting or modifying export traffic between internal components; it does not involve compromise via long-lived tokens, so this requirement does not bear on the described threat.

Customer data is written to a managed object store (evd-003, evd-006), but thr-005 concerns interception or tampering of data in transit on the path to that store, not the provider’s retention and usage terms once data is stored. Documenting external processor data handling would not prevent the network-level attack described, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

req-TPI-002 addresses bounding work triggered by external events or metered services. In the export service, work is initiated by authenticated customer export requests (evd-001–evd-004), and thr-005 concerns eavesdropping or tampering with that traffic, not unbounded triggering of work or cost, so this requirement does not bear on this threat.

The architecture does not describe any endpoint that accepts events from an external platform; instead, customers make export requests directly to the Export API (evd-001–evd-003). thr-005 focuses on interception of internal export traffic, not authenticity of inbound webhooks, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.
assumptions: Assume the export service does not expose any inbound webhook or event receiver endpoints beyond the documented Export API (evd-001–evd-003).

mappings.applicability_reason: req-WEBHOOK-002 concerns preventing or safely handling replay of inbound events. thr-005 describes an attacker with internal network access intercepting or tampering with export traffic between services, not replaying authenticated webhook events, so this requirement does not bear on the threat.

documentation_gaps.title: Protection of internal export data flows is not documented
documentation_gaps.description: The architecture and operations documentation describe the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store and the data they handle (evd-001–evd-003, evd-006), but do not state whether the internal channels between the Export API and Export Worker and between the Export Worker and the managed object store use encryption in transit or mutual authentication, nor how connectivity to the managed object store is restricted. Without this information, it is not possible to determine whether an attacker with internal network access, as assumed in thr-005, could intercept or tamper with export requests or files in transit.
documentation_gaps.importance: Needed to verify whether sensitive export data is protected in transit between internal components and to assess compliance with encryption and network-segmentation expectations relevant to thr-005 (req-DATA-001 and req-NET-001).
requested_evidence: Deployment or network architecture documentation describing how the Export API, Export Worker, and managed object store communicate on df-002 and df-003, including protocols used, whether TLS or another encryption mechanism is enabled, and whether mutual authentication is enforced.

Cloud or platform configuration showing how access to the managed object store is restricted (for example, VPC endpoints, private subnets, firewall or security-group rules, or service mesh policies) and which components are permitted to connect.

Documentation or configuration evidence establishing whether the managed object store encrypts export files at rest and, if so, which managed service provides that encryption and how it is configured.
